name: CTA Tracker
description: Live map of CTA trains and buses around one stop, with the next arrivals in each direction.
author: Ryan

milesNorth.title: Map reaches north (miles)
milesNorth.description: From the center to the top edge. 1 mile from Division is Armitage. The map's height fits north + south; its width shows whatever fits at that scale.

milesSouth.title: Map reaches south (miles)
milesSouth.description: From the center to the bottom edge. 1.25 miles from Division is Lake.

showPassed.title: Show vehicles that already passed
showPassed.description: Drawn faded. Off hides them entirely.

scaleWithSize.title: Scale with module size
scaleWithSize.description: Grow text, icons and lines with the module, so a large module stays readable from across the room. Text size still applies on top. Off sizes everything from Text size alone.

showLegend.title: Show legend and update time
showLegend.description: The line under the arrivals explaining solid, dashed and bright. Off frees the space for the map and board; errors and an out-of-date warning still show when they happen.

iconStyle.title: Vehicle icons
enumLabels: Round badges with a pointed nose
Train as a rail car, buses round
Square trains, round buses, outside arrow

nearStops.title: Emphasize buses within (stops)
nearStops.description: Buses this many stops or fewer from the center are drawn larger with a halo and a stop count. 0 turns it off.

highlightRoutes.title: Highlight approach stops for routes
highlightRoutes.description: Comma-separated. The last stops before the center on these routes are drawn bright, in both directions.

busRoutes.title: Bus routes
busRoutes.description: Comma-separated route numbers, up to 10. The stop nearest the center is used for each direction.

trainStation.title: Blue Line station ID
trainStation.description: Train Tracker map ID. Division is 40320.

positionSeconds.title: Check vehicle positions every (seconds)
positionSeconds.description: CTA publishes new bus positions about every 30 s. Markers glide between updates either way; checking more often shows each new position sooner.
